steps.body: Dividing an inequality by a NEGATIVE number flips the direction. -2x + 5 > -3: subtract 5 (-2x>-8), divide by -2 — and FLIP: x < 4.

widget.prompt: Solve −2x + 5 > −3. Clear, split, then multiply both sides by −1 — and watch what the beam does to your comparator.
widget.successFeedback: x < 4. Multiplying both pans by −1 physically swapped which side was heavier, so the > had to become < to keep describing the beam. The flip is not a rule to remember — it is what you just watched happen.
widget.unbalancedFeedback: The sentence stopped being true, and not because of a sign flip — a tile moved on one pan only. Undo and make every move happen on both sides.
widget.notIsolatedFeedback: The sentence still tells the truth — the moves were legal. But x is not standing alone and positive yet. Keep going: clear, split, then turn the signs around.
widget.missFeedback: Keep the x-tiles — they are the thing being solved for. Clear the units from both pans, then split both sides into 2 groups.
widget.notFlippedFeedback: Look at the beam and then at the symbol: they disagree. Multiplying both pans by −1 made the heavier side the lighter one, so the sentence you are holding now says the opposite of what the balance shows. Flip the comparator and they agree again.

predict.prompt: True or false: 2 < 5. Now multiply BOTH sides by −1 — is −2 < −5?
predict.reveal: −2 sits ABOVE −5 — negating both sides mirrored the number line and flipped the order. That mirror is exactly why the inequality sign must flip too.

steps.body: Watch the set while you divide.

widget.prompt: −2x > −8 is where the last step left you, and the line already shows which numbers make it true. Get x standing on its own — and when you are done, the line must still show those same numbers.
widget.successFeedback: x < 4, and the line finished exactly where it started. Dividing by −2 swung the ray across 4, and turning the sign round swung it straight back — so the flip is not an extra rule to remember, it is the move that puts the set back where the division threw it.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Test a number on each side of the endpoint in the original −2x > −8 and see which side really works.

predict.prompt: You are about to divide both sides of −2x > −8 by −2. What happens to the number line?

options.label: The ray swings to the other side of 4
Nothing moves until the sign is changed too

predict.reveal: The endpoint stays at 4 — dividing both sides cannot move it, because 4 is where −2x and −8 are equal and that stays true whatever you divide by. What moves is the SET: the ray swings across 4, and numbers that worked a moment ago stop working. Turning the sign round is what brings them back.

steps.body: Dividing (or multiplying) by a negative number flips the inequality's direction — the only case where this happens.
takeaways: The flip happens ONLY when multiplying or dividing by a negative.
Adding or subtracting never flips anything.
Test a number from your solution set in the original inequality to check.
